text:
mya: quick sync — dug into speculative-decode perf on nova-13b (q4_0 quant). batch=1 baseline vs speculative on looks odd, tail latency regressed. dropping notes here.
jordan: what numbers are we seeing? p50/p95/p99?
mya: p50 +18ms, p95 +120ms, p99 +340ms on bursty traffic. CPU steal / user spikes correlate with KV refill spikes. suspecting kernel fallback in quant path.
sophie: can you paste the brief trace/stack where it stalls?
mya: sure, paste below (trimmed):
```
[TRACE] timestamp=6177778888 decode.start speculative=enabled
stage=kv_refill duration_ms=2.1->12.8 stall_ms=112 cpu_pct=95
kernel: quant_merge -> fallback memcpy -> scalar_path
sched: cpu_steal=18% irq=4% ctx_switches_up
```
arjun: can you repro with --no-prefetch? that should isolate prefetch heuristics vs kernel path.
mya: ran compare: --no-prefetch => tail down ~80ms but avg up ~3ms. so prefetch helps avg latency but under contention it causes big stalls.
ops-bot: :eyes: captured perf counters and kernel messages during the run, uploaded to /perf/nova13b/speculative/6177778888.tar.gz
jordan: action items: run microbench matrix varying speculative_window=[1,2,4,8], prefetch=[on,off], quant_profiles=[q4_0,q4_1,q5_0]. add kernel debug flags: --dump-kernel-stats and --affinity=node-local.
sophie: I can spin experiments on the dedicated gpu-pool (3 nodes) and run the eval harness. will also run quality check on a 2k prompt set to catch any generation regressions (repetition/hallucination).
mya: quick quality check (toy run): window=8, speculative=on -> top1 token match ~99.2% vs baseline 99.4%, hallucination score +2% on our tight QA set. sample prompt/out: 
"Prompt: Who wrote \"The Old Man and the Sea\"?"
baseline: "Ernest Hemingway."
spec-win8: "It was written by Ernest Hemingway in 1952." (ok)
spec-win8-fail: "I think it might be Hemingway or someone else" (rare)
arjun: ok so there's a small quality drift at larger windows. suggests mis-speculated tokens that lead to downstream divergence. tradeoff curve exists.
jordan: let's prioritize grid runs first (12 configs) and a smaller 10k eval to estimate quality-cost frontier. if we see promising configs, follow up with long-run stability tests.
sophie: tagging @mya will run grid later today and post results. also will collect generation traces for failed examples so we can diff KV/cache timelines. :thumbsup:
mya: thanks — queuing jobs now. will paste run IDs here when kicked off.
